prize_parts.citation: for developing targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules redirect the ubiquitin-proteasome system to destroy chosen proteins

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation converts occupancy-driven inhibition into event-driven, catalytic removal of a protein, by designing molecules that bring a target and an E3 ligase together. It is a chemical design principle with a mechanistic core (ternary complexes, cooperativity, induced proximity) and it has changed what chemists and clinicians can attempt: targets without a druggable active site become approachable. Crews and Deshaies supplied the PROTAC concept and first proofs, and Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target explained the molecular-glue branch and gave the field its most widely used ligase handle. Seven of the eight opening ballots rank B045, and six of us place it in the top four, which suggests it is a broadly acceptable anchor even when it is not everyone's first choice.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC is yet an approved drug, so the clinical consequence is promised more than demonstrated, and the glue branch (thalidomide analogues) is the more mature part. Any three-name prize omits Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito, who made real contributions (VHL ligands, ternary-complex structure, first proof of concept, cereblon identification with Handa). The concept (PROTACs) and the discovery (cereblon as glue target) are also two different achievements joined under one heading, which the citation has to handle carefully.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks ionizable lipid nanoparticles first as a game-changer with global demonstrated consequences, and ranks degraders only fourth because no PROTAC has reached approval at scale.
responses.response: I agree that B009 has the stronger evidence of real-world consequence today, and I take the maturity point on PROTACs seriously. But the glue branch has already produced approved drugs, and the cereblon mechanism is well understood, so the premise that consequences are only emerging is partly overstated. I also worry about your suggested trio of Cullis, Anderson and Langer: the delivery credit is split among Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer, with patent disputes, and it is one of the harder attributions on the list. That is why I keep B009 as an alternative rather than my first choice, though I would not oppose it.

responses.point: Chabes ranks degraders first as a programmable chemical tool (induced proximity) with broad generality, noting that late-stage approval is pending and timing may be slightly early.
responses.response: I share your reading of induced proximity as a designable chemical reaction, and I think that framing is the best defence of B045 as chemistry rather than pharmacology. Where I would qualify your view is credit: you propose the same Crews, Deshaies, Handa trio, but I think we should state openly that this rewards the concept and the cereblon mechanism, not the optimisation work by Ciulli and Gray, and that the citation should be worded to match. I am less relaxed than you about timing; if the committee wants a PROTAC approval first, we should say so openly.

responses.point: Somfai ranks Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling (Buchwald, Hartwig) first as a general, ligand-designed method that is long mature, widely used in process chemistry and arguably overdue, and he ranks degraders only seventh.
responses.response: The maturity and attribution case for B069 is cleaner than mine: two clear laureates, decades of confirmation, and an area the 2010 cross-coupling prize left out. I cannot dismiss that. My disagreement is about generative potential. C-N coupling made an existing bond construction routine, whereas degraders opened a modality, and the biomedical reach is wider. If the committee prefers certainty over novelty, B069 is the safer prize, and I would regard that as a legitimate position rather than a lack of ambition.

responses.point: Sparr ranks biomolecular condensates first as a unifying physical-chemical principle (demixing, multivalency) with a quantitative framework from Rosen and the liquid-droplet demonstrations of Hyman and Brangwynne.
responses.response: I find the physical-chemical case compelling and it is closer to my own interests than many of the list. My reservation is the one you partly raise yourself: whether in vivo condensates are truly phase-separated liquids is still contested, and the credit boundary with Pappu and Mittag is unsettled. I would want the mechanism and the definition to be settled before awarding it, and a three-name cut would exclude at least two principal contributors.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept awarding degraders before a PROTAC has been approved.
How to word a citation that covers both the PROTAC concept and the cereblon/molecular-glue discovery without implying Handa's work is a PROTAC advance.
Whether excluding Ciulli and Gray, who did major optimisation and ligand work, is defensible, or whether Ciulli should replace one of the three.
I cannot independently verify the current clinical status of degraders.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile. My research is on peptides, nanoparticle biosensing and biomaterials, with no collaboration with the degrader, lipid-nanoparticle or base-editing candidates; my postdoc mentors (Stevens, Boey) are not on the shortlist. I do share some research overlap with Emma Sparr on self-assembly, which is relevant to B008 but is not a recusal-level connection.
